title: Analyze Incoming Payments
raw_text:
9/29/26, 9:48 AM

Analyze Incoming Payments

With the Analyze Incoming Payments (F5588) app, you can monitor and analyze incoming payments to optimize clarification
processes and team workload.

Key Features
You can use this app to regularly do the following:

e Analyze how many payments have been clarified manually within a given period.

e Analyze the effectiveness of the automated clarification process provided by the standard.

1 Note

If you have licensed and are using SAP Cash Application, add-on for contract accounting, you can regularly validate the
effectiveness of the applied machine learning to the clarification process.

You display the data per company code. You can refine the filter criteria as required by choosing Adapt Filters to include, for
example, the posting date, and lot type.

The app analyzes payment lots, credit lots, and check lots, and displays an overview of which amount and number of payments in a
payment lot has been cleared automatically or manually.

1 Note

If you are using SAP Cash Application, add-on for contract accounting, the app analyzes payment lots, credit lots, and check
lots, and displays an overview of which amount and number of payments in a payment lot has been cleared using machine
learning.

Views

You can display the data by using the following view options:

e The Chart View shows all payment lots matching the filter criteria.

The default dimension is Lot. The default measures are Payments in Clarification, Payments Posted Automatically,
Payments Posted Manually, and, if you are using SAP Cash Application, add-on for contract accounting, Payments Posted
Using Cash App.

e The Table View lists more details per payment lot than the Chart View, including the total number of payments in
clarification, the total number of items in lots, and the total payment amount in the last row of the table.

You can combine the table and chart view in a single display.

For each view, you can change chart, dimensions, and measures in the Settings dialog. You change the display by selecting a chart
type in combination with a dimension and measures.
